title: No diagnostics bundle exists and a shipped build persists no log at all: every Rust, sidecar and MCP line goes to process stdout, so a user with a problem has nothing to hand a maintainer
repro: grep -rniE 'diagnostic|support.?bundle|bug.?report|export.*log|collect.*logs' src sidecar src-tauri/src -> no diagnostics mechanism (only the order-audit CSV and two dead 'for diagnostics' helpers). find ~/Library/Logs, the data dir and ~/.vysted-terminal for *log* -> only audit_log.db. `log show --start '2026-09-19 06:28' --end '2026-09-19 06:36' --predicate 'process CONTAINS[c] "vysted"'` over the 19-Sep 0.8.0 boot (which provably ran: mcp-endpoint.json written 06:31:43) -> 38 lines, all Apple SkyLight/launchservices noise, 0 lines of the app's own [sidecar]/[vysted]/uvicorn output.
evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:225-238 (sidecar stdout/stderr re-printed via println!/eprintln! only), src-tauri/src/openbb_mcp.rs:125-136 (same for MCP children), src-tauri/Cargo.toml:25 (tauri features [] : no tauri-plugin-log, no devtools), sidecar/main.py:142 (uvicorn log_level only; no basicConfig/dictConfig/FileHandler anywhere in sidecar/, so service warnings use Python's lastResort handler with no timestamp), src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:1875-1880 (version string is the only diagnostic UI), docs/BLUEPRINT.md:315 (opt-in crash telemetry promised) vs README.md:5 (no telemetry); $ISO/seat-l3-diagnostics/evidence/unified-log-19sep.txt, status-endpoints.txt, canary-drive.txt
notes: Diagnosability was never designed. Output is a side effect of println! and uvicorn defaults, and the local-first no-telemetry posture removed the crash signal without a user-controlled local replacement. Consequence: every field report ('research failed', 'screener empty', 'app went blank') arrives with zero evidence, and the only way to get any is to relaunch the binary from a terminal and reproduce. The ingredients are already secret-clean, measured: 0 of 7 BYOK key canaries sent through every key path reached the log, and the 14 loopback status endpoints (/health, /system/*, /search/*, /mcp/status, /openbb-mcp/status, /sec/status, provider-health) carry no secrets or usernames. What does leak into the log stream: URL query strings (user search terms, proven with a /resolve?q= canary), symbols, and full tracebacks on a 500. Smallest fix: a size-capped rotating log file under <data-dir>/logs written by the Rust drain (tauri-plugin-log, or a file sink beside the println!), plus a Settings 'Copy diagnostics' action that bundles version + the status-endpoint JSON + a log tail with query strings, symbols, prompt/brief/note text and the public IP redacted, so the user sees it before sending.

title: No React error boundary anywhere: one panel's render throw removes the whole cockpit, and the stack goes to a console a release build cannot open
repro: design (NEEDS-GUI to demonstrate visually): src/main.tsx:17 createRoot(...).render(<StrictMode><Page/></StrictMode>) passes no onUncaughtError/onCaughtError; src/app/ holds only page.tsx + globals.css (no error boundary file); `grep -rn 'componentDidCatch|ErrorBoundary' src` -> 0 non-test hits; dockview mounts every panel via createPortal into the same root (node_modules/.pnpm/dockview@6.2.2_react@19.2.6/node_modules/dockview/dist/package/main.cjs.js, 3 createPortal sites). React's documented default: 'if your application throws an error during rendering, React will remove its UI from the screen' (https://react.dev/reference/react/Component).
evidence: src/main.tsx:17-21; src-tauri/Cargo.toml:25 (no devtools feature, so the release WKWebView console is unreachable); React docs quote above
notes: The failure is total and silent. A malformed provider payload or an unexpected null in any one of 25 panels blanks every panel, including the portfolio and chat, with no message, no recovery short of relaunch, and no captured stack (see LIFE-L3-DIAGNOSTICS-1: nothing persists). A relaunch restores the same autosave and can re-crash on the same panel. Smallest fix: wrap each dockview panel component in an error boundary (at PanelHost's component map) that renders an inline 'this panel crashed - reload panel / copy error' fallback, and pass onUncaughtError to createRoot to write the stack to the diagnostics log.
